system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Order: Tech, Energy, Wars and Markets in Tension
system_description.narrative_summary: The global system is being strained by simultaneous, interacting pressures: an accelerated AI/tech competition that destabilises markets and raises new security risks; energy and climate shocks (Middle East attacks, tanker incidents, hurricanes) that remake supply chains and political bargaining; and renewed high-intensity conflict and proxy warfare (Ukraine, Yemen, Horn of Africa) that stress alliances and institutions. Financial-market volatility (bond yields, equity rotations) and polarized domestic politics — especially in the United States — amplify short-term decision cycles, producing feedbacks across diplomacy, trade and corporate strategy.
system_description.scope: Sovereign states and alliances; major non-state actors (armed groups, tech firms, financiers); global markets (oil, bonds, equities, freight); critical infrastructure (data centres, ports, shipping, refineries); multilateral institutions and regulatory regimes; cross-border supply chains for chips, energy and food.
system_description.super_system: The integrated global socio-economic-political system (planetary-scale market, governance and environmental environment) within which states, firms and societies co-evolve.
adjacent_subsystems: International financial system and capital markets
Regional security architectures (Europe, Middle East, Indo-Pacific, Horn of Africa)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively and variably by NATO and other partners, remain locked in an intense war marked by expanding strike campaigns, reciprocal attacks and shifting battlefield dynamics and international support.

variables.name: US–China AI and chip rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China, with major global tech firms and allied markets, are contesting leadership in AI, semiconductors and data infrastructure through investment races, supply‑chain strategies and regulatory pressure that are reshaping technological dominance and economic leverage.

variables.name: Iran-proxy maritime and Gulf attacks
variables.description: Iran and its regional proxies (notably the Houthis) and Gulf states, with U.S. and international maritime interests involved, are escalating attacks on shipping and airports that are shifting the security of energy chokepoints, commercial routes and regional deterrence calculations.

variables.name: Eurozone sovereign yield stress
variables.description: Eurozone governments, the ECB and global investors are confronting a rise in sovereign yields and bond-market volatility that is shifting fiscal politics, central‑bank influence and cross‑border capital flows across Europe and beyond.

variables.name: China–Taiwan gray‑zone pressure
variables.description: China and Taiwan, with U.S. and regional security partners engaged, are seeing increased gray‑zone coercion — maritime patrols, militia presence, cyber and political pressure — that is shifting deterrence, operational risk and regional alliance calculations.
